elements.element: Customer pays no liquidated damages or penalties.
elements.evidence: The defaulting Party is expressly not liable for liquidated damages or any penalty in respect of reclaimed capacity, and amounts already paid may not be forfeited. Accrued unpaid accounts remain ordinary payment obligations, not liquidated damages or penalties.

elements.element: Any Customer-payable liquidated amount is only an early-termination fee.
elements.evidence: No Customer-payable liquidated amount exists in the rendered clause; the defaulting Party is expressly protected from liquidated damages and penalties, so the condition for this limitation is absent.

elements.element: The early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause imposes no early-termination fee, making a cap unnecessary because the condition is demonstrably absent.

elements.element: The early-termination fee is the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer.
elements.evidence: No early-termination fee or other liquidated amount is payable under the rendered clause, so the condition for this exclusivity requirement is absent.
